# CanvasElementOptions

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Options for [`CanvasElement`](canvas-element.md). The draw handler is required and stays a constructor value (it is stored `readonly`, not a settable property).

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

```typescript
type CanvasElementOptions = ElementOptions & Partial<Omit<Pick<CanvasElement, (typeof CANVAS_ELEMENT_OWN_OPTION_KEYS)[number]>, 'drawWidth' | 'drawHeight'>> & {
    /** Drawing-surface width. Accepts a length: `240`, `'8cm'`, or `{ value, unit }`. */
    drawWidth?: LengthInput;
    /** Drawing-surface height. Accepts a length: `160`, `'8cm'`, or `{ value, unit }`. */
    drawHeight?: LengthInput;
}
```

## Properties

- [`altText`](#alttext): The alternate text for this element.
- [`breakAllowed`](#breakallowed): Whether this element can be split across page boundaries.
- [`captureName`](#capturename): Optional author-supplied name/key surfaced in the layout snapshot.
- [`contentDirection`](#contentdirection): Inline progression and paragraph base direction; omitted inherits.
- [`drawHeight`](#drawheight): Drawing-surface height.
- [`drawWidth`](#drawwidth): Drawing-surface width.
- [`isDecorative`](#isdecorative): When `true`, the author has explicitly opted into a decorative-only rendering: the element is tagged as `/Artifact` with no warning, even though no alt-text is provided.
- [`keepWithNext`](#keepwithnext): Keeps this element with the start of its next sibling in vertical flow.
- [`margin`](#margin): Margin around this element.

### `altText`

```typescript
altText?: string | undefined
```

*optional*

The alternate text for this element. Empty/undefined means "no alt-text"; the renderer treats such elements as `/Artifact` rather than `/Figure` when tagging is on, and may log a warning so authors don't silently produce inaccessible figures.

### `breakAllowed`

```typescript
breakAllowed?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Whether this element can be split across page boundaries. When false, the element is treated as atomic and will be moved to a new page rather than split. If it doesn't fit on a fresh page either, it renders anyway. Default is true.

### `captureName`

```typescript
captureName?: string | undefined
```

*optional*

Optional author-supplied name/key surfaced in the layout snapshot. Unset by default; a future capture API can populate it.

### `contentDirection`

```typescript
contentDirection?: ContentDirectionInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Inline progression and paragraph base direction; omitted inherits.

### `drawHeight`

```typescript
drawHeight?: LengthInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Drawing-surface height. Accepts a length: `160`, `'8cm'`, or `{ value, unit }`.

### `drawWidth`

```typescript
drawWidth?: LengthInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Drawing-surface width. Accepts a length: `240`, `'8cm'`, or `{ value, unit }`.

### `isDecorative`

```typescript
isDecorative?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

When `true`, the author has explicitly opted into a decorative-only rendering: the element is tagged as `/Artifact` with no warning, even though no alt-text is provided. Distinguishes "missing alt by mistake" from "no alt is correct".

### `keepWithNext`

```typescript
keepWithNext?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Keeps this element with the start of its next sibling in vertical flow.

### `margin`

```typescript
margin?: ThicknessInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Margin around this element. Accepts `12`, `[h, v]`, `[l, t, r, b]` or `{ bottom: 12 }`; omitted sides are zero.
